UTILIZATION OF HIGH-FREQUENCY CORONA DISCHARGE OZONATION TECHNOLOGY IN WASTEWATER TREATMENT PROCESSES

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Maxat Mamadiyarov, Kanat Zhunussov, Yerlan Tashtay, Maigul Zhekambayeva, Yesenbekov Azamat, Zhantore Isaliyev, Saltanat Ospanova, Adilzhan Nurmolda, Abirbek Sandugash

ABSTRACT

The study examines the capacity of an ozonator system based on a high-frequency corona discharge to treat wastewater effectively. The traditional water treatment methods are underperforming due to the increasing problems of water scarcity and pollution. The high-frequency corona discharge ozonator system, in comparison to conventional methods like chemical flocculation and filtration, presents a more favorable solution in terms of energy efficiency and effectiveness of treatment. The integration with renewable energy sources can reduce energy consumption by 15% and increase ozone production efficiency by 25% as per research findings (mean ± standard deviation values were obtained from n = 3-5 repeated experiments).. By optimizing system parameters, ozone concentration of up to 38 mg/L (38 ± 1, 5 mg/L) was achieved which was capable of effectively removing pollutants from wastewater. Additionally, the research highlights the role of water quality parameter monitoring (sediment, electrical conductivity, pH) in enhancing ozone production efficiency. The experiments were carried out thrice (n = 3-5), and results are expressed as mean ± standard deviation.
